title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 187 (Definitions of express and implied authority)

content.overview: Section 187 provides that an authority is said to be express when it is given by words spoken or written. An authority is said to be implied when it is to be inferred from the circumstances of the case; and things spoken or written, or the ordinary course of dealing, may be accounted circumstances of the case.
content.glance: Express authority is given by words spoken or written. Implied authority is inferred from the circumstances of the case (including things spoken or written, or the ordinary course of dealing).
content.study: An authority is said to be express when it is given by words spoken or written. An authority is said to be implied when it is to be inferred from the circumstances of the case; and things spoken or written, or the ordinary course of dealing, may be accounted circumstances of the case. Current-law framing: statutory definitions of the two forms of authority recognised by Section 186.

sections.heading: Express authority
sections.body: An authority is said to be express when it is given by words spoken or written.

sections.heading: Implied authority
sections.body: An authority is said to be implied when it is to be inferred from the circumstances of the case; and things spoken or written, or the ordinary course of dealing, may be accounted circumstances of the case.

examples.title: Express vs implied
examples.body: Authority given by a written power of attorney is express. Authority inferred from a course of dealing is implied under Section 187.

hypotheticals.question: Authority is inferred from the ordinary course of dealing. Is it express or implied?
hypotheticals.analysis: Implied. Section 187 provides that an authority is implied when it is to be inferred from the circumstances of the case, and the ordinary course of dealing may be accounted such a circumstance.

distinctions.title: Scope of Section 187
distinctions.body: Section 187 applies only to the circumstances described in its statutory text. It does not create additional grounds or remedies beyond those stated.
